data.title: Record Football Matches With One or Two Phones | Pitchside
data.heroH1: How to record a football match your team can actually use.

contentBlocks.content: The five-minute setup before kick-off
For device-specific settings and equipment recommendations, use the complete phone recording guide.
1. Clean the lens
A fingerprint can soften the whole recording, especially under floodlights. Wipe each lens before mounting the phone.
2. Turn on Do Not Disturb
Reduce the chance that calls and notifications interrupt the recording. Confirm the device settings that work with the phone being used.
3. Check battery and storage
Allow for warm-up, stoppages, half-time and extra recording before and after the match. Do not begin with a nearly full device or a battery that only just covers the scheduled playing time.
4. Use landscape orientation
Frame the width of the playing area. Lock the phone securely so it cannot rotate during the match.
5. Record a test
Walk to both goals, move through the centre and watch the test back. If players are too small or the goal disappears, change the setup before kick-off.
Choose one phone or two
One-phone setup
Mount the phone close to halfway and above head height. Frame the entire compact pitch where possible.
Use one phone when:

items: the playing area fits clearly in the frame;
players at both ends remain large enough to see;
the group wants the simplest repeatable setup;
only one suitable device is available.

contentBlocks.content: Watch for the far-end blind spot. The phone may technically include the whole pitch while making the action too small to analyse well.
Two-phone setup
Mount both phones near halfway. Point one towards each goal and include enough overlap around the centre.
Use two phones when:

items: one angle loses goal-area detail;
the pitch is wider or longer;
players become too small at the far end;
both files can be charged, stored and uploaded reliably.

contentBlocks.content: Position the phones safely
The recording must never create a risk for players, spectators or equipment.

items: Follow venue rules before attaching anything to a fence.
Keep stands outside the playing and run-off areas.
Secure tall equipment against wind and contact.
Use a safety tether where appropriate.
Do not balance a phone loosely on a wall, bag or rail.
Stop using the setup if it cannot be made stable.

contentBlocks.content: The Pitchside double-phone mount is in development. Preorder information should be added only after its compatibility and safety requirements are approved.
Compare setup options on the football camera app page.
Press record early, then leave the phone alone
Start before kick-off so the beginning of the match is not lost. Once the angle is confirmed, avoid handling the phone unless there is a safety or recording problem.

A fixed wide view may look less dramatic than someone following the ball by hand, but it is more consistent for post-match review. Sudden pans, zooms and shakes can remove the context around an event.
At half-time:

items: confirm the recording is still running;
check the mount has not moved;
check battery and available storage;
avoid changing the angle unless the first half exposed a clear problem.

contentBlocks.content: After full-time
Stop the recording only after the final action is complete. Confirm that the file saved and keep the original footage until upload and processing have finished.
Upload through the available Pitchside workflow. If two phones were used, follow the approved file-naming and upload order shown inside the product.
During private beta, upload and processing can currently take up to 45 minutes. Connection speed, file size, video length and the developing workflow can affect the result.
The output should be reviewed before stats or clips are treated as final. Read the football video analysis workflow.
What good footage can support
Pitchside's approved launch product includes Match Stats & Highlights, Leaderboards and Personal Stats. Paid users also receive Personal Clips.
The private beta is testing supported events around goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles. Camera position and visibility can affect whether an event or player is identified correctly.
See AI football highlights for clip examples and football stats app for the player record.
Get consent before you record

Recording a match creates responsibilities for the person filming and sharing it. Check venue, league, team and participant rules before kick-off, with additional safeguards where children or vulnerable players are involved.
Read Recording Consent & Privacy. Do not treat an app signup as automatic permission to publish every participant.
Recording allowances
The Free plan includes one recording per month, Match Stats & Highlights, Leaderboards and Personal Stats.
The Paid plan includes one recording per week and Personal Clips for £4.99 weekly, £12.99 monthly or £99 annually.
Before launch, the pricing FAQ must confirm that two files from the same two-phone match count as one recording allowance.
Match-day checklist

items: ☐ Permission and venue rules checked
☐ Lens clean
☐ Battery and storage checked
☐ Do Not Disturb enabled
☐ Landscape orientation locked
☐ Phone mounted above head height
☐ Pitch and both goals visible where possible
☐ Stand, clamp and tether secure
☐ Test clip reviewed from both ends
☐ Recording started before kick-off
☐ File confirmed after full-time

Recording FAQ

faqs.answer: Yes, when one stable view clearly covers the small-sided pitch. Two phones are preferred when a single view makes the far end too small or misses important detail.
faqs.question: Can I record a football match with one phone?
Where should I put the phone?
faqs.answer: Start near halfway, above head height and outside the playing area. Test the complete pitch view before kick-off and follow the venue's safety rules.
Publish tested settings by phone type in the detailed recording guide. Do not give one universal resolution, frame-rate or storage estimate without device-specific testing.
faqs.question: Which camera settings should I use?

faqs.answer: This needs confirmation before launch. The intended customer expectation should be that two files from one match count as one match recording, but do not publish that promise until Dave approves the product rule.
faqs.question: Does two-phone recording use two allowances?

faqs.answer: Keep every saved section and follow the upload guidance in the app. Do not guarantee that incomplete footage can be combined or fully analysed until the workflow supports it.
faqs.question: What if the recording stops?

tldrPoints: Clean the lens, enable Do Not Disturb, check battery and storage, use landscape and record a test.
Use one phone for a clearly covered compact pitch or two phones for stronger goal-area detail.
Keep mounts outside the playing area and follow venue safety rules.
Confirm the saved file, upload through Pitchside and review output before treating it as final.
Check recording consent and confirm how two-phone files count against plan allowances before launch.
data.aeoQuickAnswer: To record a football match your team can use, place a phone near halfway, raise it above head height, lock it in landscape orientation and test both ends of the pitch before kick-off. One phone can cover a compact pitch; two phones improve far-end and goal-area detail. Check safety, battery, storage and consent before recording.

technologyStack.title: Computer Vision for Small-Sided Football
technologyStack.desc: Pitchside is being developed around phone-recorded small-sided football footage, where camera angles, lighting and player spacing are different from professional broadcast footage.

technologyStack.title: Event Detection in Testing
technologyStack.desc: The beta system is being tested to identify goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles from match footage, with accuracy expected to improve as more footage is reviewed.

technologyStack.title: Phone-First Recording
technologyStack.desc: Pitchside aims to offer a phone-first workflow for teams that do not want to invest in dedicated football-camera hardware.

technologyStack.title: Edge-to-Cloud Pipeline
technologyStack.desc: Uploads and processing are being tested during private beta. Current processing can take up to 45 minutes and the flow is expected to improve.

data.metaDescription: Set up one or two phones to record a 5-a-side, 6-a-side or 7-a-side match. Check position, blind spots, battery, storage and what happens after upload.
data.llmDescription: This match-day guide explains how to record 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side football with one or two phones for Pitchside. It covers lens cleaning, Do Not Disturb, battery and storage, landscape orientation, test recordings, safe phone positioning, half-time checks, upload, consent and Free or Paid recording allowances. Detailed equipment recommendations remain in the separate phone-recording guide.
data.intro: Get the phone high, keep it steady and make sure the pitch stays in view. That matters more than owning the newest camera. Pitchside works with suitable phone-recorded 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side footage. Use this page as the short match-day setup. For detailed equipment recommendations, settings and affiliate links, use the complete phone recording guide.
